title: Latent change sandboxing notes — quick checklist & follow-ups
content:
Quick context and intent:
This is a personal scratchpad for thinking through safety nets when landing latent/behavioural changes that are low-risk in code size but have outsized surface in runtime behavior (KV-cache handling, batching heuristics, token accounting, minor kernel reorderings). Goal: a compact checklist that I can copy into PR descriptions + a short runbook for early follow-ups and metrics to watch.

Notes to self (top-level thoughts):
- Small code delta + big behavioral risk: prioritize layered safety (unit tests -> integration -> narrow canary -> rollout).
- Avoid full-service toggles if we can do request-scope toggles or per-model gating — easier rollback.
- Prefer metric-based rollback triggers (explicit thresholds) over manual eyeballing.

Pre-merge checklist to put in PR description:
- [ ] Unit tests cover edge cases (KV miss/hit toggles, cold vs warm cache)
- [ ] Add a tiny integration that simulates 1K warm requests and 1K cold requests (local harness)
- [ ] Bench: include p50/p95/p99 token latency and tokens/sec baseline vs new change (CI artifact)
- [ ] Note compatibility: which models/quantizations this touches (list in PR)
- [ ] Add a feature flag scoped to route/model (e.g., feature.latent_reorder=model_x) with default off
- [ ] Add a short “how to reproduce locally” (docker-compose or test harness cmd)
- [ ] Add a short “how to reproduce locally” (docker-compose or test harness cmd)

Canary rollout plan (narrow-scope):
- Phase A (internal): route 5% of internal-synthetic traffic (non-customer) for 24h.
  - Validate correctness (sample logs) and perf (p95 baseline).
- Phase B (alpha customers): 1–2 trusted customers / 2–4 routes, 1% traffic for 24–48h.
- Phase C (gradual increase): double every 24h while alerts are green, up to 25% then 50% then full (if comfortable).

Immediate monitoring & alerting (create before merge):
- Latency: p95 token generation latency change > +15% -> SEV-3 (investigate)
- Throughput: tokens/sec drop > 20% for 10m window -> alert
- Error rate: increase in 5xx or model inference errors > 0.5% absolute -> alert
- Cost: GPU utilization change > 10% sustained -> notify infra
- Quality: automated evals on a small prompt set (10–20 prompts) — BLEU/ROUGE-ish or human-read flag sample mismatch > threshold -> warn

Fallback & rollback plan (explicit steps):
1) Flip feature flag to previous state (per-route if possible).
2) If flag flip doesn’t resolve, route traffic to previous model variant / compatible fallback (route policy).
3) If degradation persists, halt autoscaler changes and open incident page.
4) Reproduce locally with recorded trace from problematic request id.

Local repro snippets (notes):
- Run small harness: python tools/run_batch_sim.py --routes example_route --requests 2000 --seed 42
- Capture KV cache warmup: export KV_LOG=1 && ./bin/infer --model=xxx --trace=trace.json
- Quick perf: hyperfine 'curl localhost:8080/v1/generate -d @sample.json' -w '...'%

Testing matrix (quick):
- Models: small/medium/large (quantized/float16) — smoke on each
- Sequence lengths: 64, 512, 2048 — ensure KV eviction behavior is sane
- Batch shapes: 1, 4, 16 — reveal batching regressions
- Cold vs warm: measure first-token vs after 50 tokens

Follow-ups after merge (first 72 hours):
- [ ] Add per-route dashboard tiles: p50/p95 latency, errors, tokens/sec
- [ ] Snapshot cost delta for the new config and attach to PR thread
- [ ] Collect 100 random responses from canary and do quick quality pass (manual)
- [ ] If any alert fires, annotate incident in PR and link timeline
- [ ] Write a short blurb for the release notes about the change and mitigation knobs

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve (notes for pairing or async):
- Can we make the per-request toggle both fast and low-overhead? current implementation uses atomic bool but some hot paths may still check config object (microcost).
- Are we confident the CI perf harness is representative? might need a tiny dedicated e2e in staging with real model weight (not a stub).
- How to instrument per-token accounting without high cardinality metrics explosion? consider percentiles with tags (model, route) instead of per-request time series.

Non-blocking nice-to-haves (later):
- Auto-bisection script that runs binary search on rollouts to find traffic point where metric deviates.
- Add a tiny smoke lambda that runs the 20-sample eval every 30 minutes and posts digest to slack.

Scratch TODOs (for me):
- [ ] Add the reproduce commands to template PR checklist (copy to repo/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md)
- [ ] Wire up the p95 alert in Grafana (dashboard id TBD)
- [ ] Pair with Maya to verify integration test harness covers sequence length 2048 case

Random reminders:
- Keep PR descriptions short + link to this note for details.
- When requesting review, ping at least one person who knows the batching/caching code (Evan) and one SRE for perf signals (Maya).

End of scratchpad. Will trim and copy relevant parts into PR when ready.
